name: Rava Fish Fry
cuisine: Konkan coast (Maharashtrian Malvani / Mumbai, Goan and Mangalorean)

ingredients.name: Seer fish / kingfish steaks (surmai), with skin and centre bone
Semolina, fine or medium (rava / sooji)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 2 tbsp used (3 tbsp on the plate)

ingredients.name: Kashmiri red chilli powder, for the coating
Sunflower or other refined oil (or coconut oil, the Mangalorean choice)
Lemon wedge and onion rings, to serve (optional, not counted in nutrition)

equipment: Flat tawa or heavy non-stick frying pan (24 cm), for shallow-frying
Flat spatula (a thin steel one slides under the crust without tearing it)
Two plates: one for the semolina coating, one lined with paper towel for draining
Small mixing bowl and spoon, for the marinade; measuring spoons; kitchen towel or paper towel for drying the fish
Optional: air fryer (see the Low-oil variant)

steps.title: Rinse the fish
steps.text: Rinse the 2 surmai steaks (150 g) under cold running water, gently rubbing off any scales near the skin.
steps.tip: Wash your hands, board and knife with soap after handling raw fish.
steps.visualCue: Clean, shiny steaks with no blood spots around the bone
steps.cameraCheck: The rinsed steaks on a plate
steps.videoShot: Water running over two fish steaks in a colander.

steps.title: Dry the fish
steps.text: Pat both sides dry with a kitchen towel or paper towel.
steps.tip: Wet fish makes the marinade runny and the crust soggy.
steps.visualCue: The surface looks matt, not wet
steps.videoShot: A towel pressing on a fish steak.

steps.title: Make the marinade
steps.text: In a bowl, mix 5 g (1 tsp) ginger-garlic paste, 5 ml (1 tsp) lemon juice, 0.5 g turmeric, 3 g (1 tsp) Kashmiri chilli powder, 1 g (½ tsp) coriander powder, 0.5 g (¼ tsp) garam masala and 1.5 g (¼ tsp) salt into a thick paste.
steps.visualCue: A thick, brick-red paste that holds on the spoon; add ½ tsp water only if it will not spread
steps.videoShot: A spoon stirring a red masala paste.

steps.title: Coat with the marinade
steps.text: Rub the paste on both sides and the edges of each steak.
steps.visualCue: No white flesh showing; an even red layer
steps.videoShot: Fingers spreading red masala over a fish steak.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Cover and leave the fish to marinate.
steps.visualCue: The masala looks absorbed and slightly drier
steps.videoShot: A lid placed over the marinated fish.

steps.title: Mix the coating
steps.text: On a flat plate, mix 30 g (3 tbsp) semolina, 5 g (2 tsp) rice flour, a pinch of chilli powder and a tiny pinch of salt.
steps.cameraCheck: The coating mix on the plate
steps.videoShot: Fingers tossing semolina and rice flour together.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Put the tawa on medium-high heat and add 15 ml (1 tbsp) oil; spread it with the spatula.
steps.tip: A hot pan in the first few seconds is what makes the crust crisp (My Food Story); if the rava does not sizzle, wait.
steps.visualCue: The oil shimmers and a pinch of semolina sizzles at once
steps.videoShot: A pinch of rava sizzling in hot oil.

steps.title: Coat the first steak
steps.text: Press one steak into the semolina on both sides and the edges, then shake off the loose grains.
steps.visualCue: A thick, even crust with no red patches
steps.videoShot: A fish steak pressed into semolina, then flipped.

steps.title: Coat the second steak
steps.videoShot: Two crusted steaks side by side.

steps.title: Place in the pan
steps.text: Lay both steaks in the hot oil, a little apart, and lower the heat to medium.
steps.visualCue: A steady sizzle all round the edges
steps.videoShot: Steaks laid gently into sizzling oil.

steps.title: Fry the first side
steps.text: Leave them alone; do not move or flip.
steps.tip: Flipping too early tears the crust; wait until it lets go of the pan by itself.
steps.visualCue: The bottom edges turn golden-brown and the steak releases when nudged with the spatula
steps.cameraCheck: The edge of a steak lifted to show the crust
steps.videoShot: The spatula lifting a corner to show a golden crust.

steps.title: Flip
steps.text: Turn each steak carefully with the flat spatula. If the pan looks dry, add 1 tsp oil around the edges (counted in the 15 ml).
steps.videoShot: A steak flipped to show the golden side.

steps.title: Fry the second side
steps.text: Fry on medium heat until the second side is golden.
steps.visualCue: Both sides golden-brown; the flesh at the bone is opaque white, not translucent, and flakes when pressed with a fork
steps.cameraCheck: A fork pressing the flesh near the bone
steps.videoShot: A fork flaking white flesh next to the bone.

steps.title: Drain
steps.text: Lift the steaks onto the paper-lined plate.
steps.visualCue: A little oil soaks into the paper; the crust stays crisp
steps.cameraCheck: The steaks on the paper towel
steps.videoShot: Golden steaks set down on a paper towel.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Plate the fish with a lemon wedge and onion rings and eat at once.
steps.visualCue: A crunchy, golden crust with a red rim of masala
steps.videoShot: A squeeze of lemon over a crisp fish steak.

reasons: lean fish gives about 30 g protein, omega-3 fats, vitamin D and B12 for about 330 kcal, with only about 10 ml oil absorbed and low saturated fat. Points come off for sodium (about 900 mg), refined semolina, almost no vegetables, and mercury in large fish like surmai. Restaurant versions often deep-fry or use much more oil on the tawa, more salt, and sometimes reused oil.

researchRating.basis: a signature dish of Mumbai Malvani, Goan and Mangalorean seafood cooking, on the menu of almost every coastal-food restaurant in Mumbai and Pune, named in Mumbai seafood guides (rava-fried bombil at Chaitanya and Gomantak restaurants in Homegrown and Migrationology), and published by every major Indian recipe site. Published recipe ratings are positive but low-volume: Madhura's Recipe 4.5/5 (4 votes) and 5/5 (1 vote), Raksha's Kitchen 5/5 (3 votes), Kitchen of Debjani no reviews; that is the small deduction, along with frequent complaints of soggy or falling-off crusts at home.

storage: Best eaten fresh; the crust softens within an hour. Leftovers: cool within 1 hour, refrigerate in a closed box for up to 1 day. Not recommended for freezing once fried (the crust goes soggy); raw marinated fish can be frozen for up to 1 month and coated just before frying. Reheat once on a dry tawa or in an air fryer at 180 °C for 3–4 min per side until steaming hot (a microwave makes the crust soggy).
leftoverRemix: Fish fry pav or wrap. Flake the fish off the bone, warm it on a tawa, and stuff it into a buttered pav or a roti with green chutney, sliced onion and a squeeze of lemon, like a Mumbai fish pav. Use within the 1-day window.
burnOff: about 4.7 km of running (330 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 6.6 km of brisk walking (about 80 minutes at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). Rice or curry on the side is extra.

navratri.reason: contains fish, garlic, wheat rava and table salt, all avoided under the common Navratri vrat rule set.

ekadashi.reason: contains fish and wheat rava (grains are avoided on Ekadashi under the common rule set).

jain.reason: contains fish, plus garlic and fresh ginger (roots).

ramadan.reason: seafood needs no halal slaughter, so there is no sourcing swap (same rule as earlier FitPlate seafood dishes). A good high-protein iftar side with rice and dal or curry; at about 900 mg sodium (est.) it is a little salty for sehri unless you cut the salt.

jain.reason: contains fish, plus garlic and fresh ginger (roots).

pescatarian.reason: fish is the only animal food; no meat, egg or dairy.

glutenFree.reason: rava (semolina) is wheat; the Gluten-free variant below swaps it for rice rava. This recipe uses no hing.

dairyFree.reason: no curd, butter, ghee or milk.

variants.reason: the Jain diet excludes fish; the dish is defined by the fish.
